text:
kevin: heads-up — p95 latency spike on dedicated qwen->mixtral speculative pairing. started after yesterday's kernel selector tweak.

maria: wow. numbers?

kevin: p95 went from 88ms -> 120ms on 512 token median seq, small batch (1-4). CPU spike on tokenizer & kv lookup. trace:
```
[profile] kernel_selector: choose=conv_fused for qwen; fallback=mha_generic for mixtral
[serve] kv_lookup_ms=23 -> 48
[decode] speculative_accept_rate=0.22 -> 0.09
```

ash: speculative_accept_rate drop is worrying — are we hitting tokenizer mismatch? qwen vs mixtral tokenizers have different BPE vocab alignments.

lia: did we change RoPE scaling or heads mapping? I remember a RoPE scale patch in the hull branch.

kevin: yes, we applied uniform RoPE scale normalization 0.9 for cross-family pairing. maybe that's causing more rejections in draft acceptance check.

sam: what's the acceptance check logic today? I thought it's logprob + token overlap threshold.

maria: correct: acceptance if delta_logprob < 0.7 AND top_token_overlap >= 0.5. That overlap metric uses tokenizer identity; mismatch reduces overlap.

ash: that explains drop. If tokenizer outputs different splits, overlap metric is meaningless across families. We should fallback to language-model agreement on detokenized text for cross-family pairs.

kevin: quick experiment: disabled overlap check for qwen->mixtral pairing and kept logprob only. p95 improved to 96ms and accept_rate to 0.31.

lia: nice. But watch for hallucination regressions. We should add a normalized detokenized similarity check (edit distance or BLEU) as a fallback.

maria: agree. Also the kernel selector change: conv_fused was chosen for qwen but mixtral's optimized kernels aren't compatible and we hit a slower generic path. Need kernel compatibility tags in selector.

sam: propose action items:
- revert kernel-selector rule until compatibility matrix updated (kevin)
- disable tokenizer-overlap for cross-family pairing and add detok-sim (ash)
- add perf test for small-batch p95 with speculative on dedicated (lia)
- run end-to-end eval to detect quality regressions (maria)

kevin: assigned. I'll push a revert + canary tonight.

dev-bot: deployment started: canary to dedicated pool id d-11

ash: FYI, KV cache invalidation pattern also changed after the RoPE scale patch — we were conservatively flushing KV on family switch; that adds 8-12ms.

maria: can we keep KV across family switch if head/kv dims match? need a safe handshake check: (dims==dims && rope_compat==true)

lia: I'll add a handshake RPC that returns kernel_tags, kv_dims, rope_scale_hint.

sam: once we have that, kernel selector can use handshake to avoid bad fallbacks.

kevin: ok. timeline: revert and canary now, perf test tomorrow, handshake + token-sim next week.

lia: cheers. leaving a note in eng-runtime for tracking.

kevin: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
